summary: Backend-only regression for CI slice fix + Feb-2026 data-integrity sprint. Fast slice (default addopts `-m "not slow"`) completes in 18.45s with 800 passed / 0 failed / 0 xfailed — well under the 60s target and the 20-min workflow ceiling. Slow gate runnable via explicit `-m slow -o addopts='-n 2 --dist loadscope'` (3 corpus-determinism tests pass in 0.79s; corpus-coverage file also carries the marker). All 8 sprint tests in test_feb2026_sprint.py pass. Live API verified against /api/rc5/golden/summary (all new fields present: category_coverage=15 cats, latency dict with p50/p95/mean, mitre_technique_count=14, mitre_technique_ids sorted, has_data=true, total=88, pass_rate=100.0), /api/rc5/golden/history?limit=3 (ascending ts, p50/p95/mean/mitre_technique_count/pass_rate all present per entry), /api/benchmark/cache/stats shape correct with all 6 keys, two sequential /real-world calls produced exactly 1 miss + 1 hit (hit_rate=0.5), key=(mtime_ns, corpus_len). Cache invalidation verified via unit test (test_invalidate_forces_miss + test_mtime_change_invalidates_cache). Parse regression sanity: benign cmd echo → Benign / T1059 / cmd LOLBAS; iwr downloader → Suspicious / T1105; reflective load → T1620 Reflective Code Loading. Sprint additions are purely additive and non-regressive.

minor.issue: Live call from preview URL exceeded 120s wait window; refresh_once() triggers real OSINT feed pulls (MalwareBazaar 401 seen in backend logs). Cache-invalidation side-effect is fully covered by unit tests; only the outer /refresh HTTP wrapper is slow. Not caused by this sprint.

action_items: Optional: Skip corpus_refresh.refresh_once() when NIVXRAY_OFFLINE=true or add a 15s outer timeout to /api/benchmark/refresh so pod-facing curl doesn't hang when external feeds throttle. Not blocking for the CI slice fix.
Restoring `CI=true craco build` (mentioned as P1 pending) is a frontend concern and outside this backend-only iteration.
critical_code_review_comments: pytest.ini addopts include `-m "not slow"` — this is a *default* filter; any developer running `pytest -m foo` will unknowingly OR it with `not slow`. Considered acceptable since the marker's intent is exactly that (opt-in only), but worth a comment in pytest.ini for future maintainers.

routers/benchmark.py::_invalidate_cache does not reset hits/misses counters intentionally so telemetry survives invalidations — matches unit-test expectation (test_invalidate_forces_miss asserts hits=1, misses=2). Good.

routers/rc5_golden.py::golden_summary correctly returns empty containers + has_data=False when no run exists (safety net verified). category_coverage/latency/mitre fields align 1:1 with GoldenRunReport.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing golden corpus + persisted golden runs in Mongo.
context_for_next_testing_agent: CI slice baseline is now 800 passed in ~18s with `-m "not slow"` (default). Slow-marked files: test_corpus_determinism.py, test_corpus_coverage.py. Full gate is `-m 'slow or not slow'` (nightly). Golden summary/history include mitre_technique_count/ids + latency dict. Benchmark cache key = (REPORT_JSON.mtime_ns, len(CORPUS)), stats endpoint public at /api/benchmark/cache/stats. Live /api/benchmark/refresh can be slow (>120s) due to OSINT feed calls — prefer unit tests for cache-invalidation coverage.
rca of the issue: n/a — regression verification only, no bug reproduced.
